searchText: Has anyone done work on handling "dust" ETH balances and in ERC20 contracts? Could we define a storage type in solidity with some configurable magnitude value that would round "dust" eth/token balances to 0 and thus not have to be stored anymore? I think this was done at some ETH upgrade HF in the past, but it was a one time thing and only for ETH balances? Having trouble finding the reference now. I'm somewhat interested (but strapped for time) to analyze how much state storage could be freed by this. Here's a blast from the past: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/issues/168 I think many of the concerns could be fixed by making the "dust" cleaning configurable. e.g. Dollar tokens would probably use a much higher limit than WETH. And this also makes it possible for ERC20 tokens to get this "Dust" handling behavior in a gas efficient way.
